page: Amazon Web Services m5n.24xlarge is a general-purpose, network and EBS-optimized server instance. It is powered by the Nitro hypervisor and features an x86_64 architecture with an Intel Xeon 8259CL processor. The configuration includes 96 dedicated virtual CPUs, which correspond to 48 physical cores with 2.0 threads per core, running at a clock speed of 3.1 GHz. The CPU features 32 KB L1d cache, 1.0 MB L2 cache, and 35 MB L3 cache, with support for AVX, AVX-512F, AVX-512 VNNI, and AES instructions.

The instance is equipped with 384.0 GB of DDR4 memory running at 3 GHz, providing 4.0 GB of RAM per core. It does not include local storage, requiring reliance on network-attached EBS volumes. For network connectivity, the instance delivers a baseline network bandwidth of 100 Gbps, though it includes zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Performance benchmarks reveal a distinct contrast between single-core and multi-core capabilities. Single-core stress-ng and gzip compression benchmarks fall into the bottom 25%, indicating limited single-threaded performance. Conversely, multi-core stress-ng, Passmark CPU, and Passmark CPU extended instructions tests rank in the top 25%. Memory bandwidth tests also show strong results, with read-only small block cached speeds reaching 4502.67 GB/sec and uncached large block write speeds at 94.12 GB/sec. Redis SET operations are highly efficient, processing 74.81 million operations per second. However, LLM text generation benchmarks are weak to poor, with the 7B model achieving only 5.67 tokens per second.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the m5n.24xlarge offers high resource density and substantial memory bandwidth, making it suitable for workloads that can leverage its 96 vCPUs and 100 Gbps network capacity. The lack of local storage and weak single-core performance are key tradeoffs. This instance is best suited for multi-threaded workloads, database operations, static web serving, and network-intensive applications, rather than single-threaded tasks or large-scale LLM text generation.
